brief.lead_headline: Dispatch logs 47 commits in a single day as audio, podcast, and admin architecture converge
brief.lead_body: Dispatch had its busiest single day on record. Forty-seven commits resolved a run of audio routing failures, graduated the podcast subsystem from scaffolding to a coherent feature, and closed the day by migrating project management logic out of the admin panel and into individual project pages.

mentioned_in_briefings.excerpt: AI SDK landed Claude Platform on AWS, a gateway serviceTier option, and Vercel access token support while closing two Anthropic tool bugs.
AI SDK shipped two new providers and a clutch of provider fixes across 31 commits and two releases — the window's single busiest project by volume.
AI SDK logged the highest commit count at 34, adding Gemini 3.5 Flash, a Cerebras provider, and managed-agents support.
Twenty-two commits landed in AI SDK today, delivering the Vue useChat composable, sandboxed file I/O wrappers, and a same-day Vertex project-ID backport alongside a Node 22 floor.
Thirty commits landed in AI SDK today, anchoring on a patch for Google's Interactions API before its upstream breaking change hits on May 26.
Astro cut two patch releases and cleared a backlog of correctness bugs in MDX, the Node adapter, and redirect handling.
Astro pushed astro@6.3.6 and @astrojs/cloudflare@13.5.3 before noon, then spent the afternoon closing gaps in Vite build-option inheritance and Cloudflare SSR optimizeDeps forwarding.
Astro cut 6.3.4 and 6.3.5 within three hours, bundling a stale-content dev-server fix, CSP correction, and a full error-message overhaul.
Astro added one item — a Vite race condition dropping React in dev mode — and every other project was silent.
Astro's busiest concern was a security patch: unescaped slot names in hydration attributes opened an XSS vector, closed at 13:32 and released as `astro@6.3.3` minutes later.
Upstream, Claude Code closed roughly a hundred issues in a sweep around 22:30 UTC while fresh bugs around ECONNRESET, PTY CPU spin, and --resume fork selection queued up.

Claude Code's tracker saw a bulk closure of roughly fifty issues around 22:35, with new reports arriving through the night on MCP respawn failures, credential detection, and a word-boundary fix for the @claude trigger.
Claude Code pushed two releases but absorbed more issues than it closed — stale daemons, a context-spec regression, and a broken worktree attach path among them.
Claude Code shipped nothing substantive but drew a cluster of agent-mode reports worth reviewing before that surface sees wider use.

Claude Code shipped v2.1.143 quietly but opened six bug reports by day's end, including a 429-into-400 retry spiral that leaves sessions unrecoverable and a Task tool gap that collapses multi-agent orchestration to single-agent execution.
Dispatch had its busiest single day on record.
Seven commits landed in Dispatch overnight, covering the podcast page redesign, split-deployment CORS support, and the long-form brief mode generating this issue.

Nine commits took Dispatch from skeleton to deployable: Phases 2–7 landed together, followed by a configurable scheduler, a manual trigger, a backfill script, and an architectural note pinning Caddy as the gateway.

Dispatch left the marklab monorepo this morning as its own repository, with backend and frontend reorganized under apps/ and a Phase 1 foundation plan drafted, executed, and archived in seventeen commits.
Metaflow drew a security disclosure — four findings, one an RCE claim — low in volume, not in consequence.
Metaflow closed the night with 2.19.29.
Metaflow absorbed four merged PRs in a tight early-morning window, closing bugs ranging from an orphaned-process race condition to a Windows SIGALRM crash in the timeout decorator.
Workflow SDK worked both ends of the day: replay-stability commits in the early hours, then three production fixes and a v4 wire-format migration by evening.
Workflow SDK cut beta.6 with a graphile-worker schema bootstrap and a socket fix, while a new issue immediately flags Cloudflare Workers as blocked on node:vm.

Fourteen commits landed in Workflow SDK today, anchored by a fix to `formatDurationPrecise` — which had been producing boundary nonsense like "60s" and "1m 60s" — subsequently folded into `formatDuration` as a precise mode.
